effective_date_basis: Buprofezin has been identified by EFSA as an endocrine disruptor; the European Commission issued a draft non-approval decision and, as of the most recent SCoPAFF meeting found in research for this forecast (9-10 July, year of that meeting not independently confirmed beyond the source used), proposed extending the interim approval to 31 December 2026 pending a formal non-approval vote expected within 2026. The exact effective date of the eventual withdrawal-of-authorisation deadline is NOT yet fixed; 31 December 2026 is used here as the latest known backstop date, not a confirmed non-renewal effective date. This uncertainty is itself part of the forecast and should be scored accordingly.
destination_reasoning: Brazil is documented (Public Eye, "Banned in Europe") as the second-largest global recipient of EU-banned pesticides historically (~10,000 tonnes in 2018), across many substance classes, making it a high base-rate prediction for any new EU pesticide restriction. Viet Nam and Thailand are added on agronomic grounds specific to this substance rather than the general base-rate pattern: buprofezin is an insect growth regulator whose major documented agricultural use is against rice planthoppers, and Viet Nam and Thailand are among the largest rice-growing countries with no equivalent EU-style restriction, unlike the more generic destination list used for the flufenacet forecast below.

effective_date_basis: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/910 of 20 May 2025 non-renewed flufenacet; Member States had to withdraw authorisations by 10 December 2025, with any Member-State grace period for existing stocks required to expire by 10 December 2026 at the latest (Article 46 of Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009). The substantive EU market exit therefore completes by this date at the latest -- this forecast predicts what is observable in trade data by then, not a still-undecided regulatory outcome like buprofezin above; it is included to test the scoring mechanism on a case with a firm legal deadline rather than only on a genuinely uncertain one.
destination_reasoning: Ukraine is documented (Public Eye, "Banned in Europe") as the third-largest recipient of EU-banned pesticides by 2018 (~5,000 tonnes across six agrochemicals) and is a major wheat/barley producer -- flufenacet is specifically a cereal herbicide, so this is not just the generic high-risk-destination base rate but a substance-specific agronomic match. Brazil is included on the same general base-rate grounds as in the buprofezin forecast.
